title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. For the first two-dimensional sketch, draw the first face by creating a loop that starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and draws a line to (0.1449, 0.0), then to (0.1449, 0.007), and back to the origin. Repeat this process for the second two-dimensional sketch, ensuring the dimensions and coordinates are identical. Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.1449. Transform the scaled sketch into three dimensions by applying the same Euler angles and translation vector used initially. Extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular prism should be a length of 0.1448598130841121, a width of 0.0070093457943925215, and a height of 0.75.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch points
points = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.1449, 0.0),
    (0.1449, 0.007),
    (0.0, 0.007)
]

# Create the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").polyline(points).close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular prism
r = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is now represented by 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a workplane on the XZ plane
result = cq.Workplane("XZ")

# Draw a rectangle with width along X (0.1449) and height along Z (0.7500)

# Extrude along Y (thickness 0.0070)

import cadquery as cq

# Thin plate with rounded short ends (stadium profile), extruded vertically
r = cq.Workplane("XY") \
     .moveTo(0.0035, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1414, 0.0) \
     .threePointArc((0.1449, 0.0035), (0.1414, 0.007)) \
     .lineTo(0.0035, 0.007) \
     .threePointArc((0.0, 0.0035), (0.0035, 0.0)) \
     .close() \
     .extrude(0.75)
